standard.name: Canonical affine form of the exact survival factor model

assumptions.condition: The primitive centered donor operator \(\mathcal C_D\) has exactly \(d=r-1\) nonzero singular directions, with rank zero interpreted literally when \(r=1\).
For fixed \(0<\gamma_-\le\gamma_+<\infty\), every nonzero singular value of \(\mathcal C_D\) lies in \([\gamma_-,\gamma_+]\) when \(d>0\).
For fixed \(0<\kappa_-\le\kappa_+<\infty\), every eigenvalue of \(\int_{\mathcal I}b_0(t)b_0(t)^\top\,dt\) lies in \([\kappa_-,\kappa_+]\) when \(d>0\).

For \(d=r-1\) and \(d\ge1\), let \(z_m^{(N,d)}\) be obtained, for each \(N\ge2d+1\), by empirical Gram--Schmidt from the explicitly centered columns
\[
 q_{k,m}^{(N)}=\{m-(N+1)/2\}^k-N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{N}\{\ell-(N+1)/2\}^k,
 \qquad 1\le k\le d,
\]
and define \(R_d=\sup_{N\ge2d+1}\max_{1\le m\le N}\|z_m^{(N,d)}\|_2\), with \(R_0=0\), let \(\Phi_d\) be the deterministic \(L^2(\mathcal I)\)-orthonormalization of \(\psi_\circ,t\psi_\circ,\ldots,t^{d-1}\psi_\circ\), with first coordinate \(\psi_\circ/\|\psi_\circ\|_2\), and put \(A_{p,d}=a_{\circ,p}\|\psi_\circ\|_2\Phi_d\), and suppose the fixed primitive constants obey
\[
 g_-\le1,
 \qquad
 R_d\le M_z,
 \qquad
 \gamma_-^2\le(a_{\circ,0}^2+a_{\circ,1}^2)\|\psi_\circ\|_2^2\le\gamma_+^2,
 \qquad
 \kappa_-\le a_{\circ,0}^2\|\psi_\circ\|_2^2\le\kappa_+,
\]
\[
 \max_{p\in\{0,1\}}\sup_{t\in\mathcal I}\|A_{p,d}(t)\|_2\le M_b,
 \qquad
 2|a_{\circ,0}|h_\circ c_f^{-1/2}
 \left\{\int_0^{\bar\tau}\{\psi_\circ'(t)\}^2dt\right\}^{1/2}
 \le\frac34(1/2-\alpha),
\]
and, writing \(v_\circ=|a_{\circ,1}|/4\), for every \(p\in\{0,1\}\), every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\) with \(\|x\|_2\le R_d\), every \(|v|\le v_\circ\), and every \(t\in\mathcal I\), the curve
\[
 \ell_{p,x,v}(t)=e^{-\lambda_\circ t}+A_{p,d}(t)^\top x+\mathbf 1\{p=1\}v\psi_\circ(t)
\]
satisfies
\[
 s_-\le\ell_{p,x,v}(t)\le1,
 \qquad
 -\partial_t\ell_{p,x,v}(t)\ge0,
 \qquad
 \inf_{t\in\operatorname{supp}(\psi_\circ')}[-\partial_t\ell_{p,x,v}(t)]\ge c_f,
 \qquad
 \left\|-\frac{\partial_t\ell_{p,x,v}}{\ell_{p,x,v}}\right\|_{C^\beta(\mathcal I)}\le L;
\]
and for \(d=0\), the same four inequalities hold with the empty factor term, \(x=0\), and every \(|v|\le v_\circ\).

definitions.name: Canonical normalized survival-factor coordinates
definitions.construction: Set \(s_p(t)=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}S^0_{p,m}(t)\). Write the singular-value decomposition of the primitive centered operator as \(\mathcal C_D=\sum_{k=1}^d\sigma_k u_k\otimes v_k\), ordered by decreasing \(\sigma_k\) with deterministic sign and tie-breaking rules. Define \(z_{m,k}=\sqrt{N_0}v_{k,m}\) and \(b_{p,k}(t)=\sigma_k u_{k,p}(t)\), so \(N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}z_mz_m^\top=I_d\). Define the shared target coordinate \(z_\star\) by the unique coefficient equation \(S^0_{0,\star}-s_0=b_0^\top z_\star\). Then \(S^0_{p,m}(t)=s_p(t)+b_p(t)^\top z_m\), \(s_p(0)=1\), and \(b_p(0)=0\). When \(d=0\), all vectors, sums, and Gram matrices in this construction are zero-dimensional.

definitions.name: Exact-rank censored Synthetic Survival Control class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)=\{P_{N_0,K_T,K_D}: P_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\text{ satisfies }\mathrm{ass:control-consistency},\mathrm{ass:patient-independence},\mathrm{ass:independent-censoring},\mathrm{ass:censor-overlap},\mathrm{ass:event-overlap},\mathrm{ass:hazard-smoothness},\mathrm{ass:normalized-factor-model},\mathrm{ass:exact-centered-rank},\mathrm{ass:centered-contrast-spectrum},\mathrm{ass:pre-contrast-gram},\mathrm{ass:donor-incoherence},\mathrm{ass:target-loading-bound},\mathrm{ass:factor-envelope}\}\). Exact rank is imposed on the primitive operator \(\mathcal C_D\); for \(r=1\), its rank is zero and every contrast-space object uses the zero-dimensional convention.

definitions.name: Per-triple uniform continuous-time honesty class
definitions.construction: For each evaluated triple, define \(\mathcal H_r(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)=\{B:\inf_{P\in\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)}P\{B^{\mathrm{lo}}(t)\le\theta(t)\le B^{\mathrm{up}}(t)\text{ for every }t\in\mathcal I\}\ge1-\alpha-\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)\}\). Thus admissibility is enforced at the same triple at which width is evaluated, while \(\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)\) vanishes uniformly on every three-dimensional tail.

definitions.name: Explicit normalization-preserving fixed-rank target-loading pairs
definitions.construction:
Fix \(d=r-1\).  For every integer \(N_0\ge2d+1\) and \(1\le k\le d\), define the explicitly centered donor column
\[
 q_{k,m}=\{m-(N_0+1)/2\}^k-
 N_0^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{N_0}\{\ell-(N_0+1)/2\}^k,
 \qquad 1\le m\le N_0.
\]
Apply deterministic empirical Gram--Schmidt to \(q_1,\ldots,q_d\) in the inner product \(N_0^{-1}\sum_m xy\), orienting each column to have positive leading polynomial coefficient, and denote the resulting row vectors by \(z_m^{(N_0,d)}\).  Thus every column is mean zero and \(N_0^{-1}\sum_m z_m^{(N_0,d)}z_m^{(N_0,d)\top}=I_d\); for \(d=1\), \(z_{m,1}^{(N_0,1)}=\{m-(N_0+1)/2\}/\sqrt{(N_0^2-1)/12}\).

For \(d\ge1\), apply deterministic \(L^2(\mathcal I)\) Gram--Schmidt to \(\psi_\circ,t\psi_\circ,\ldots,t^{d-1}\psi_\circ\), orient the first function as \(\varphi_{1,d}=\psi_\circ/\|\psi_\circ\|_2\), write \(\Phi_d=(\varphi_{1,d},\ldots,\varphi_{d,d})^\top\), and set
\[
 A_{p,d}(t)=a_{\circ,p}\|\psi_\circ\|_2\Phi_d(t).
\]
For \(u\in\{-1,+1\}\), take \(s_p(t)=e^{-\lambda_\circ t}\), \(b_p=A_{p,d}\), donor loadings \(z_m=z_m^{(N_0,d)}\), and target loading \(z_\star^{(u)}=u h_\circ K_T^{-1/2}e_1\).  Put
\[
 S_{p,m}^{(r,u)}(t)=s_p(t)+A_{p,d}(t)^\top z_m,
 \qquad
 S_{p,\star}^{(r,u)}(t)=s_p(t)+A_{p,d}(t)^\top z_\star^{(u)}
\]
on \(\mathcal I\), continue every curve after \(\bar\tau\) by its value at \(\bar\tau\) times \(e^{-\lambda_\circ(t-\bar\tau)}\), take \(C_{p,m,j}=\infty\), and let \(P_{r,u}\) be the induced independent observed-data law.  For \(r=2\), define \(P_u=P_{2,u}\).  When \(d=0\), all score arrays and factor terms are empty and the same prescription defines the homogeneous backbone.  This construction only names the laws; centering, empirical Gram, class membership, rank, spectrum, separation, and divergence are properties to be proved.

definitions.name: Rate-matched interpolation grid
definitions.construction: Choose a deterministic grid \(\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\) containing \(0\) and \(\bar\tau\) whose mesh satisfies \(h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{\min\{\beta+1,2\}}\le\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\), and use piecewise-linear interpolation between adjacent grid points.

definitions.name: Censoring-aware functional-PCR martingale-multiplier band
definitions.construction:
Let \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}:C(\mathcal I)\to C(\mathcal I)\) be the deterministic piecewise-linear interpolation operator on \(\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\). For a population panel set
\[
 \widetilde S^0_{p,m}=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}S^0_{p,m},
 \qquad
 \widetilde s_p=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\widetilde S^0_{p,m},
 \qquad
 \widetilde Y_m=(\widetilde S^0_{0,m}-\widetilde s_0,
                         \widetilde S^0_{1,m}-\widetilde s_1),
\]
and \(\widetilde\Gamma=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\widetilde Y_m\otimes\widetilde Y_m\). Apply the same selected positive-square-root factor map and pre-period least-squares map described below to \((\widetilde S^0_{p,m})\), with the same fallback rule, and denote the resulting total population comparison curve by \(\theta^{\mathrm{pop}}_{r,\mathcal G}\). For \(r=1\), set \(\theta^{\mathrm{pop}}_{1,\mathcal G}=\widetilde s_1\). This comparison curve is a proof object defined through the interpolated \(L^2\) factor map; it is not a data-dependent estimator and it does not redefine the causal target \(\theta\).

On the grid, compute every full-cell Kaplan--Meier curve \(\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{p,m}\), using the convention that an empty product is one, and extend it by \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\). For \(r=1\), define \(\widehat\theta_1\) as the Kaplan--Meier curve obtained by pooling the \(N_0K_D\) donor-post records.

For \(r\ge2\), split each donor-period patient set deterministically into odd and even indices. If both folds are nonempty, compute the two fold-specific Kaplan--Meier curves, interpolate them by \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\), center each fold across donors to obtain joint-period curves \(\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\) and \(\widehat Y_m^{(2)}\) in \(L^2(\{0,1\}\times\mathcal I)\), and form the self-adjoint finite-rank operator
\[
 \widehat\Gamma=\frac{1}{2N_0}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}
 \left\{\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\otimes\widehat Y_m^{(2)}+
 \widehat Y_m^{(2)}\otimes\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\right\}.
\]
Order its eigenvalues \(\widehat\lambda_1\ge\widehat\lambda_2\ge\cdots\), use a deterministic lexicographic sign and basis rule, and define \(\widehat\mu_k=\sqrt{\max\{\widehat\lambda_k,0\}}\). Let \(\widehat u_k\) be the corresponding joint-period eigenfunctions and set \(\widehat b_{p,k}(t)=\widehat\mu_k\widehat u_{k,p}(t)\) for \(1\le k\le d\). Put \(\widehat s_p=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{p,m}\) and \(\widehat H_0=\int_{\mathcal I}\widehat b_0(t)\widehat b_0(t)^\top dt\). On the regular event that both folds are nonempty,
\[
 \widehat\lambda_d\ge\gamma_-^2/4,
 \qquad
 \widehat\lambda_d-\widehat\lambda_{d+1}\ge\gamma_-^2/4,
 \qquad
 \lambda_{\min}(\widehat H_0)\ge\kappa_-/4,
\]
define
\[
 \widehat z_\star=\widehat H_0^{-1}\int_{\mathcal I}\widehat b_0(t)
 \{\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{0,\star}(t)-\widehat s_0(t)\}\,dt,
 \qquad
 \widehat\theta_r=\widehat s_1+\widehat b_1^\top\widehat z_\star.
\]
Equivalently, this fitted curve is the coordinate-free selected-square-root map from the interpolated empirical panel to the post-period prediction; it is invariant to rotations inside a tied selected eigenspace. If a fold is empty or any displayed threshold fails, set \(\widehat b_0=\widehat b_1=0\), \(\widehat z_\star=0\), and define \(\widehat\theta_r\) to be the pooled donor-post Kaplan--Meier curve. Thus \((\widehat s_p,\widehat b_p,\widehat z_\star,\widehat\theta_r)\) and all derivatives used below are uniformly bounded measurable functions of every dataset.

On the regular event, differentiate this rotation-invariant interpolated-input map, including the selected spectral projector and positive square-root, with respect to every cellwise product-limit counting-process increment. On the fallback event, define the empirical derivative to be the ordinary pooled Kaplan--Meier derivative. Replace each patient contribution by \(\xi_{p,m,j}\) times that contribution, and let \(c_r^\xi\) be the conditional \(q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\)-quantile of its grid supremum, where
\[
 q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}=1-\alpha+
 \min\left\{\frac{\alpha}{2},\frac{\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)}{2}\right\}.
\]
Let \(\widetilde\theta_r\) be the pointwise projection of \(\widehat\theta_r\) onto \([0,1]\), with value one imposed at zero. With \(q=\min\{\beta+1,2\}\), \(c_{\mathrm{int}}=c_{\mathrm{int}}(L,\bar\tau,\beta)\) from \(\mathrm{prop:grid\mbox{-}interpolation}\), and
\[
 A_r=c_r^\xi+\mathbf 1\{r\ge2\}\eta_D(K_D)
     +\omega_r(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)
     +c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q},
\]
define the grid endpoints by
\[
 \widehat B_r^{\mathrm{lo}}(g)=\max\{0,\widetilde\theta_r(g)-A_r\},
 \qquad
 \widehat B_r^{\mathrm{up}}(g)=\min\{1,\widetilde\theta_r(g)+A_r\}.
\]
Interpolate both endpoints linearly and impose the common value one at zero. This total measurable construction defines \(\widehat B_r\) and its multiplier process for every dataset. The allowance \(\eta_D\) is the exact deterministic half-fold risk-exhaustion envelope, \(\omega_r\) is the finite-tail nonlinear-remainder and multiplier-transfer buffer, and the discrepancy between \(S^0\) and \(\widetilde S^0\) away from the grid enters only through the final interpolation term in \(A_r\).

definitions.name: Normalization-preserving rank-adaptation handle
definitions.construction: Use a patient-martingale estimate of the second normalized contrast singular value to test exact rank one against separated rank-two alternatives, and invert that test to switch between the rank-one and rank-two oracle multiplier bands while preserving \(S(0)=1\). The threshold and the adaptive band are to be derived from the composite testing problem rather than fixed in advance.

definitions.name: Separately normalized rank-at-most-two closure
definitions.construction:
For each sample-size triple, define
\[
\mathfrak Q_{\leq 2}(N_0,K_T,K_D)
=\left\{Q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}:Q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}
\text{ has the properties below}\right\}.
\]
Every member satisfies
\(\mathrm{ass:control\mbox{-}consistency}\),
\(\mathrm{ass:patient\mbox{-}independence}\),
\(\mathrm{ass:independent\mbox{-}censoring}\),
\(\mathrm{ass:censor\mbox{-}overlap}\),
\(\mathrm{ass:event\mbox{-}overlap}\), and
\(\mathrm{ass:hazard\mbox{-}smoothness}\), with the common constants appearing in
those assumptions.  Set, canonically,
\[
s_{p,Q}(t)=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}S^0_{p,m}(t).
\]
There is a contrast indicator \(e_Q\in\{0,1\}\).  If \(e_Q=0\), then
\[
S^0_{p,m}(t)=s_{p,Q}(t)
\quad\text{for all }p\in\{0,1\},\ m\in\mathcal M,\ t\in\mathcal I.
\]
If \(e_Q=1\), there are scalar continuous factor curves \(b_{p,Q}\) and scalar
loadings \(\zeta_{m,Q}\) such that
\[
S^0_{p,m}(t)=s_{p,Q}(t)+b_{p,Q}(t)\zeta_{m,Q},
\quad
N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\zeta_{m,Q}=0,
\quad
N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\zeta_{m,Q}^2=1.
\]
The sign is selected canonically by requiring the first nonzero value in a fixed
countable dense sequence of continuous linear probes of
\((b_{0,Q},b_{1,Q})\) to be positive.  The invariant upper and loading bounds are
\[
0<\int_{\mathcal I}\{b_{0,Q}(t)^2+b_{1,Q}(t)^2\}\,dt\leq\gamma_+^2,
\qquad
0<\int_{\mathcal I}b_{0,Q}(t)^2\,dt\leq\kappa_+,
\]
\[
\max_{p\in\{0,1\}}\sup_{t\in\mathcal I}|b_{p,Q}(t)|\leq M_b,
\qquad
\max_{m\in\mathcal D}|\zeta_{m,Q}|\leq M_z,
\qquad
|\zeta_{\star,Q}|\leq M_\star.
\]
Thus every heterogeneous member has a unique target-pre coefficient, but the
definition imposes no common positive lower bound on its scalar pre-period Gram
\(\int_{\mathcal I}b_{0,Q}^2\).  All rank labels in this definition refer to the
separately normalized contrast indicator \(e_Q\), not to the fixed-rank law symbol
\(\mathfrak P_r\).

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_1(N_0,K_T,K_D)\), the canonical contrast dimension is \(d=0\), so \(S^0_{p,m}(t)=s_p(t)\) for every unit and \(\theta(t)=s_1(t)\). Along every regular submodel whose target-pre marginal law is fixed and which perturbs \(\theta\) through the post-control law, the score contribution of the target-pre records is identically zero. For fixed \(r\ge2\), any normalization-preserving loading path \(z_{\star,\eta}=z_\star+\eta v\) that remains in \(\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\) has target derivative \(\left.\partial_\eta\theta_\eta(t)\right|_{\eta=0}=b_1(t)^\top v\), which is nonzero exactly when \(b_1^\top v\not\equiv0\) on \(\mathcal I\).
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_1(N_0,K_T,K_D)\).  Since \(d=r-1\), exact rank one gives \(d=0\).  Equivalently, \(\mathcal C_D\) has rank zero by \(\mathrm{ass:exact\mbox{-}centered\mbox{-}rank}\).  Under the zero-dimensional convention in \(\mathrm{def:canonical\mbox{-}factorization}\), the inner product \(b_p(t)^\top z_m\) is an empty sum and hence is zero.  Substitution into \(\mathrm{ass:normalized\mbox{-}factor\mbox{-}model}\) gives, for every \(p,m,t\),
\[
 S^0_{p,m}(t)=s_p(t)+b_p(t)^\top z_m=s_p(t).
\]
The target definition then yields
\[
 \theta(t)=S^0_{1,\star}(t)=s_1(t).
\]

Let \(\{P_\eta:|\eta|<\eta_0\}\) be a regular submodel covered by the claim, and write \(q_{0,\star,\eta}\) for the density of one target-pre record with respect to a common dominating measure.  The target-pre marginal is fixed along this path, so \(q_{0,\star,\eta}=q_{0,\star,0}\).  Its score is therefore
\[
 \left.\partial_\eta\log q_{0,\star,\eta}(O_{0,\star,j})\right|_{\eta=0}=0.
\]
Patient independence makes the target-pre sample score the sum of these zero contributions.  This proves the stated ancillarity for precisely the paths quantified in the corrected claim.

Finally fix \(r\ge2\) and a loading path \(z_{\star,\eta}=z_\star+\eta v\) that remains in the model.  The donor loadings and factor curves are fixed, so the primitive donor operator, its rank, and its singular values are fixed.  Endpoint normalization is preserved because \(b_1(0)=0\) in the canonical factorization.  Differentiating the target formula gives
\[
 \left.\partial_\eta\theta_\eta(t)\right|_{\eta=0}
 =\left.\partial_\eta\{s_1(t)+b_1(t)^\top(z_\star+\eta v)\}\right|_{\eta=0}
 =b_1(t)^\top v.
\]
This derivative is a nonzero element of \(C(\mathcal I)\) if and only if \(b_1^\top v\not\equiv0\). \(\square\)
statements.justification: The zero-dimensional collapse and the conditional loading derivative isolate the algebraic source of the rank discontinuity.
statements.gap: HanShah2025SSC imposes exact rank but does not separate normalization or state this score degeneracy.
statements.consumer: The result tells analysts exactly which target-pre paths are ancillary at rank one.

statements.statement:
Put \(n_D=N_0K_D\), let \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\) be piecewise-linear interpolation on \(\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\), and center the functional-PCR map at the interpolated population panel \(\widetilde S^0=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}S^0\) defined in \(\mathrm{def:fpcr\mbox{-}multiplier\mbox{-}band}\). Uniformly over \(P\in\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\) and all sequences with \(\min\{N_0,K_T,K_D\}\to\infty\), there are independent mean-zero censoring-martingale influence processes \(\phi_{T,j}\) and \(\phi_{D,p,m,j}\), a deterministic grid function \(\mathfrak b_r\), and a remainder \(Q_r\) such that, simultaneously for \(g\in\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\),
\[
 \widehat\theta_r(g)-\theta(g)=Z_r(g)+\mathfrak b_r(g)+Q_r(g),
 \qquad
 Z_r=\mathbf 1\{r\ge2\}K_T^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_T}\phi_{T,j}
     +n_D^{-1}\sum_{p,m,j}\phi_{D,p,m,j},
\]
where \(\phi_{T,j}\equiv0\) when \(r=1\) and
\[
 \|\mathfrak b_r\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}
 \le \mathbf 1\{r\ge2\}\eta_D(K_D).
\]
The interpolated population comparison equals \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\theta\), and hence equals \(\theta\) at every grid point. For every sufficiently large evaluated triple, the finite-tail buffer and the conditional multiplier critical value in \(\mathrm{def:fpcr\mbox{-}multiplier\mbox{-}band}\) obey
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_r}P\{\|Q_r\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}>\omega_r/2\}
 \le\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)/4,
\]
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_r}P\{\|Z_r\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}>c_r^\xi+\omega_r/2\}
 \le\alpha-\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)/4.
\]
Moreover \(\omega_r=o(\rho_r)\) uniformly on every three-dimensional tail without a restriction on the relative growth of \(K_T\) and \(N_0K_D\). The expansion and both tail inequalities are gridwise; the interpolation perturbation inside the \(L^2\) factor map is used to establish spectrum and Gram stability, while the discrepancy between \(S^0\) and \(\widetilde S^0\) away from the grid is carried only by \(c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{\min\{\beta+1,2\}}\) in the continuous-time band.
statements.justification: The expansion composes product-limit martingales with a stable interpolated-population functional-PCR map and exposes the two independent uncertainty channels.
statements.gap: Existing survival multiplier and PCR perturbation results do not jointly control interpolation inside the censored counterfactual factor operator, its deterministic risk-exhaustion bias, and finite-tail quantile transfer.
statements.consumer: It supplies the feasible gridwise approximation and explicit buffers needed for honest continuous-time inference.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Write \(n_D=N_0K_D\), \(k_D=\lfloor K_D/2\rfloor\),
\(\varepsilon=\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)\), and
\(q_\beta=\min\{\beta+1,2\}\).  Define
\[
 a_T(K_T)=K_T^{-1/6}\log^2(e+K_T),
 \qquad
 a_D(n_D)=n_D^{-1/6}\log^2(e+n_D),
\]
\[
 \chi_r=\mathbf 1\{r\ge2\}K_T^{-1/2}a_T(K_T)
       +n_D^{-1/2}a_D(n_D)+\rho_r\eta_D(K_D),
\]
and
\[
 v_r=\mathbf 1\{r\ge2\}
 \{K_T^{-1}+N_0^{-1/2}K_D^{-1}+e^{-c_0K_T}\}
 +n_D^{-1}+e^{-c_0n_D}.
\]
By the definition of the finite-tail buffer,
\[
 \omega_r=C_\omega\{\varepsilon^{-1}\chi_r
                   +\varepsilon^{-1/2}v_r\}.                 \tag{1}
\]

Let \(\widetilde S^0=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}S^0\), and let
\(\theta^{\mathrm{pop}}_{r,\mathcal G}\) be the interpolated population
comparison in \(\mathrm{def:fpcr\mbox{-}multiplier\mbox{-}band}\).  By
\(\mathrm{lem:interpolated\mbox{-}population\mbox{-}fpcr\mbox{-}stability}\),
\[
 \|\widetilde\Gamma-\Gamma\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le C h^{q_\beta},
 \qquad
 \lambda_d(\widetilde\Gamma)\ge\gamma_-^2/2,
 \qquad
 \lambda_{\min}(\widetilde H_0)\ge\kappa_-/2,              \tag{2}
\]
for all sufficiently large triples when \(d>0\), and
\[
 \theta^{\mathrm{pop}}_{r,\mathcal G}(g)=\theta(g)
 \quad\text{for every }g\in\mathcal G.                     \tag{3}
\]
The zero-dimensional versions of (2)--(3) apply when \(d=0\).  The mesh
condition gives \(h^{q_\beta}\le\rho_r\to0\).  Hence the population point
at which the functional-PCR map is expanded lies in a fixed regular
neighborhood, uniformly over the model class.  In particular, (2), rather
than gridwise equality alone, controls interpolation inside the \(L^2\)
factor map.

Apply
\(\mathrm{lem:kaplan\mbox{-}meier\mbox{-}risk\mbox{-}exhaustion}\) to every
full donor cell, both deterministic donor folds, and the target-pre cell.
For a cell containing \(k\) patients, that lemma gives the exact identity
\[
 \widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}-\widetilde S^0
 =k^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^k\varphi_j+b_k+q_k
 \quad\text{in }\ell^\infty(\mathcal I),                   \tag{4}
\]
where the influence processes are independent and mean zero,
\[
 \|b_k\|_\infty\le C_0e^{-c_0k},
 \qquad
 E\|q_k\|_\infty^2\le C_0k^{-2}.                           \tag{5}
\]
The centering in (4) is exact because all four terms on its left and right
are acted on by the same deterministic interpolation operator.  Thus no
off-grid interpolation term is inserted into the internal covariance
operator.

For the full-cell donor means, centering at \(\widetilde s_p\), (4)--(5)
and the cross-donor remainder bound in the same lemma give
\[
 \widehat s_p-\widetilde s_p
 =n_D^{-1}\sum_{m,j}\varphi^s_{p,m,j}+b^s_p+q^s_p,
 \qquad
 \|b^s_p\|_\infty\le C e^{-c_0K_D},
 \qquad
 E\|q^s_p\|_\infty^2\le C N_0^{-1}K_D^{-2}.                \tag{6}
\]
The target-pre curve has the analogous expansion with deterministic bias
at most \(Ce^{-c_0K_T}\) and centered remainder with squared supremum norm
at most \(CK_T^{-2}\).

For each donor fold write
\[
 \widehat Y_m^{(a)}=\widetilde Y_m+U_m^{(a)}+b_m^{(a)}+q_m^{(a)},
 \qquad a\in\{1,2\}.                                        \tag{7}
\]
The two processes \(U_m^{(1)}\) and \(U_m^{(2)}\) are independent mean-zero
martingale averages because the split uses disjoint patients.  Censoring
overlap, event overlap, the hazard bound, and (4)--(5) imply
\[
 \sup_m E\|U_m^{(a)}\|_2^2\le CK_D^{-1},
 \qquad
 \sup_m\|b_m^{(a)}\|_2\le Ce^{-c_0k_D},
 \qquad
 \sup_m E\|q_m^{(a)}\|_2^2\le CK_D^{-2}.                   \tag{8}
\]
Expanding the symmetrized cross-fold operator about
\(\widetilde\Gamma\) gives
\[
 \widehat\Gamma-\widetilde\Gamma=\mathbb L_D+E_D,          \tag{9}
\]
where \(\mathbb L_D\) is the average of the terms
\(\widetilde Y_m\otimes U_m^{(a)}+U_m^{(a)}\otimes
\widetilde Y_m\).  The stability lemma bounds
\(\sup_m\|\widetilde Y_m\|_2\), and patient independence and the martingale
isometry yield
\[
 \|\mathbb L_D\|_{\mathrm{HS}}=O_P(n_D^{-1/2})              \tag{10}
\]
uniformly over the class.  Cross-fold independence gives
\(E(U_m^{(1)}\otimes U_m^{(2)})=0\), while independence across donors gives
\[
 E\left\|N_0^{-1}\sum_mU_m^{(1)}\otimes U_m^{(2)}
   \right\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2
 \le C N_0^{-1}K_D^{-2}.                                   \tag{11}
\]
The same calculation for terms containing \(q_m^{(a)}\), together with
(5), gives
\[
 \|E_D\|_{\mathrm{HS}}
 \le C\eta_D(K_D)+O_P(N_0^{-1/2}K_D^{-1}).                 \tag{12}
\]
This is the point at which cross-folding removes the same-fold
errors-in-variables expectation but does not remove the deterministic
product-limit risk-exhaustion bias.

Represent the fitted curve by the selected spectral projector, its positive
square root, and the inverse pre-period Gram matrix.  The spectral contour
identity used in the stability lemma and the algebraic identity
\[
 A^{-1}-B^{-1}=A^{-1}(B-A)B^{-1}                             \tag{13}
\]
show from (2) that this rotation-invariant composite map is twice
Fr\'echet differentiable throughout a fixed neighborhood of the
interpolated population panel.  Its first two derivative norms are bounded
by a constant depending only on the fixed class constants and \(r\).
Internal selected-eigenspace ties do not alter the composite prediction.
Equations (6)--(12), \(N_0,K_T,K_D\to\infty\), and
\(\eta_D(K_D)\to0\) also imply that the empirical regular event has
probability tending to one uniformly; on its complement the definition is
the bounded pooled fallback.

Taylor expansion at \(\widetilde S^0\), followed by (3), gives in
\(\ell^\infty(\mathcal G)\)
\[
 \widehat\theta_r-\theta
 =D_T\mathcal F_{\mathcal G,\widetilde S}
   \left[K_T^{-1}\sum_j\varphi_{0,\star,j}\right]
 +D_D\mathcal F_{\mathcal G,\widetilde S}
   \left[n_D^{-1}\sum_{p,m,j}\varphi_{p,m,j}\right]
 +\mathfrak b_r+Q_r.                                        \tag{14}
\]
Define \(\phi_{T,j}\) and \(\phi_{D,p,m,j}\) by the two displayed
derivatives, including the deterministic fold weights.  Patient
independence makes the target and donor arrays mutually independent and
mean zero.  When \(r=1\),
\(\mathrm{lem:normalization\mbox{-}collapse}\) and the explicit pooled
branch give \(D_T\mathcal F_{\mathcal G,\widetilde S}=0\), and hence
\(\phi_{T,j}\equiv0\).  Choose the fixed \(C_\eta\) in the definition of
\(\eta_D\) larger than the product of the half-fold bias constant in (5)
and the uniform derivative envelope.  Equations (5)--(12) then give
\[
 \|\mathfrak b_r\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}
 \le\mathbf 1\{r\ge2\}\eta_D(K_D).                        \tag{15}
\]
The integral Taylor remainder, the centered second-order terms in
(6)--(12), and the bounded fallback yield
\[
 \sup_P E_P\|Q_r\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}^2
 \le C\left[
 \mathbf 1\{r\ge2\}\{K_T^{-2}+N_0^{-1}K_D^{-2}
                         +e^{-2c_0K_T}\}
 +n_D^{-2}+e^{-2c_0n_D}
 \right]
 \le C v_r^2.                                                \tag{16}
\]
Since (1) implies \(\omega_r\ge C_\omega v_r/\sqrt\varepsilon\),
Markov's inequality and a sufficiently large fixed \(C_\omega\) give
\[
 \sup_P P\{\|Q_r\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}>\omega_r/2\}
 \le\varepsilon/4.                                          \tag{17}
\]

It remains to compare the oracle first-order process with the conditional
patient multiplier.  Censor overlap bounds all counting-process
integrands, and the nested time-indexed martingale class has, after
normalizing each channel by its standard-error scale, an \(L^2\)-net with
cardinality at most \(C\delta^{-2}\).  Construct dyadic nets with mesh
\(2^{-\ell}\), truncate each normalized patient contribution at level
\(k^{1/6}/\log(e+k)\), and replace the truncated patients one at a time by
their Gaussian-multiplier counterparts.  Taylor's formula for a
one-Lipschitz ramp, summed over the nets, bounds the target replacement
error by
\[
 C K_T^{-1/2}a_T(K_T),
\]
and the donor replacement error by
\[
 C n_D^{-1/2}a_D(n_D).
\]
The discarded tails are bounded by the same quantities: square-integrable
martingale increments and the stated truncation level give a factor
\(k^{-1/6}\), while summing the dyadic net maxima contributes at most the
two logarithmic factors in \(a_T\) and \(a_D\).  This derivation uses only
the bounded predictable integrands supplied by censor overlap and the
independence of patient records.

The empirical derivative differs from the oracle derivative at
\(\widetilde S^0\) by at most \(C\eta_D(K_D)\) after its centered stochastic
part has been included in (16).  Since the first-order process has scale
\(\rho_r\), independence and the triangle inequality therefore give the
one-sided Lipschitz comparison error
\[
 C\chi_r=C\left\{\mathbf 1\{r\ge2\}K_T^{-1/2}a_T(K_T)
 +n_D^{-1/2}a_D(n_D)+\rho_r\eta_D(K_D)\right\}.              \tag{18}
\]
Apply the ramp which is one below the conditional multiplier critical
value and zero one buffer unit above it.  By the definition of the
conditional quantile and (18),
\[
 \sup_P P\!\left\{\|Z_r\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}>
 c_r^\xi+\frac12\omega_r\right\}
 \le1-q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}+\frac{2C\chi_r}{\omega_r}.             \tag{19}
\]
For every sufficiently large triple, \(\varepsilon<\alpha\), and hence
\(q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}=1-\alpha+\varepsilon/2\).  Increasing \(C_\omega\)
makes the last ratio in (19) at most \(\varepsilon/4\), so the right side
is at most \(\alpha-\varepsilon/4\).  The ramp argument requires no uniform
anti-concentration constant; such a constant would fail at the
variance-zero normalization point \(t=0\) and when one information channel
is degenerate.

Finally, \(\varepsilon^{-1}\) grows no faster than an iterated logarithm of
\(a=\min\{N_0,K_T,K_D\}\).  Channel by channel,
\[
 \frac{K_T^{-1/2}a_T(K_T)/\varepsilon}{K_T^{-1/2}}
 =\frac{K_T^{-1/6}\log^2(e+K_T)}{\varepsilon}\to0,
 \qquad
 \frac{n_D^{-1/2}a_D(n_D)/\varepsilon}{n_D^{-1/2}}
 =\frac{n_D^{-1/6}\log^2(e+n_D)}{\varepsilon}\to0,          \tag{20}
\]
and
\[
 \frac{K_T^{-1}/\sqrt\varepsilon}{K_T^{-1/2}}
 =\frac{K_T^{-1/2}}{\sqrt\varepsilon}\to0,
 \qquad
 \frac{N_0^{-1/2}K_D^{-1}/\sqrt\varepsilon}{n_D^{-1/2}}
 =\frac{K_D^{-1/2}}{\sqrt\varepsilon}\to0,
 \qquad
 \frac{n_D^{-1}/\sqrt\varepsilon}{n_D^{-1/2}}
 =\frac{n_D^{-1/2}}{\sqrt\varepsilon}\to0.                 \tag{21}
\]
The exponential terms divided by their corresponding standard-error
channels tend to zero, and
\[
 \frac{\rho_r\eta_D(K_D)/\varepsilon}{\rho_r}
 =\frac{C_\eta e^{-c_0\lfloor K_D/2\rfloor}}{\varepsilon}
 \to0.                                                       \tag{22}
\]
The convergence in (20)--(22) is uniform on every three-dimensional tail:
\(a\le K_T\), \(a\le K_D\), and \(a\le n_D\), while a negative power or an
exponential dominates the iterated logarithm uniformly above \(a\).
Equations (1) and (20)--(22) prove \(\omega_r=o(\rho_r)\) without comparing
\(K_T\) with \(n_D\).  Equations (3), (14)--(19) prove all remaining
assertions.  The off-grid difference between \(S^0\) and
\(\widetilde S^0\) never enters (14); it is carried only by the explicit
interpolation allowance in the continuous-time band. \(\square\)

statements.statement: For all sufficiently large \(N_0\ge2\), \(K_T\), and \(K_D\), the two laws in \(\mathrm{def:rank-two-lecam-pair}\) belong to \(\mathfrak P_2(N_0,K_T,K_D)\), have \(S_{p,m}^{(u)}(0)=1\), and differ in observed law only through the \(K_T\) target-pre failure times. Their target curves obey \(\|\theta_+-\theta_-\|_\infty=2|a_{\circ,1}|h_\circ\|\psi_\circ\|_\infty K_T^{-1/2}\). Their likelihood divergence satisfies \[D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_+\|P_-)\le K_T\int\frac{(f_{0,\star}^{(+)}-f_{0,\star}^{(-)})^2}{f_{0,\star}^{(-)}}\,dt\le\frac{4a_{\circ,0}^2h_\circ^2}{c_f}\int_0^{\bar\tau}\{\psi_\circ'(t)\}^2dt.\] A fixed sufficiently small \(h_\circ\) therefore yields uniformly bounded total variation while preserving exact total rank two, the donor contrast-spectrum bounds, the pre-contrast Gram bounds, and endpoint normalization.
statements.justification: The worked pair audits survival validity, exact rank, separation, and likelihood distance.
statements.gap: CattaneoFengTitiunik2021 has no normalization-preserving censored functional subexperiment.
statements.consumer: The pair supplies the target-pre channel in the minimax converse.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Here \(r=2\) and \(d=1\).  Empirical Gram--Schmidt in
\(\mathrm{def:rank\mbox{-}two\mbox{-}lecam\mbox{-}pair}\) gives
\[
 N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}z_m=0,
 \qquad
 N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}z_m^2=1,
 \qquad
 \max_m|z_m|<\sqrt3\le R_1\le M_z.                         \tag{1}
\]
Since \(A_{p,1}=a_{\circ,p}\psi_\circ\), the centered donor operator has
exactly one nonzero singular value
\[
 \left\{(a_{\circ,0}^2+a_{\circ,1}^2)
              \|\psi_\circ\|_2^2\right\}^{1/2},             \tag{2}
\]
and the pre-factor Gram is
\[
 a_{\circ,0}^2\|\psi_\circ\|_2^2.                          \tag{3}
\]
The numerical inequalities in
\(\mathrm{ass:explicit\mbox{-}witness\mbox{-}compatibility}\) place (2)
and (3) in the required spectrum and Gram intervals and verify the donor
loading and factor-envelope bounds.

Since \(M_\star>0\), for all sufficiently large \(K_T\),
\[
 h_\circ K_T^{-1/2}\le\min\{M_\star,R_1\}.                  \tag{4}
\]
Apply the four pointwise compatibility inequalities with \(x=z_m\) for
donors and \(x=z_\star^{(u)}\) for the target.  They give valid
nonincreasing survival curves, event overlap, the failure-density floor on
\(\operatorname{supp}(\psi_\circ')\), and the \(C^\beta\) hazard bound.
Every factor curve and \(\psi_\circ\) vanish at zero, so
\(S_{p,m}^{(u)}(0)=1\).  Taking censoring identically infinite gives
\(G=1\), independent censoring, and censor overlap.  The product construction
gives patient independence and control consistency.  Equations (1)--(4)
verify every remaining defining property of
\(\mathfrak P_2(N_0,K_T,K_D)\).  Thus
\(P_-,P_+\in\mathfrak P_2(N_0,K_T,K_D)\).

Only the target loading changes with \(u\), and the target-post control
cohort is not observed.  Hence the observed laws differ only through the
\(K_T\) target-pre records.  The first factor coordinate gives
\[
 \theta_+(t)-\theta_-(t)
 =2a_{\circ,1}h_\circ K_T^{-1/2}\psi_\circ(t),               \tag{5}
\]
and therefore
\[
 \|\theta_+-\theta_-\|_\infty
 =2|a_{\circ,1}|h_\circ\|\psi_\circ\|_\infty K_T^{-1/2}.    \tag{6}
\]
The two target-pre densities satisfy
\[
 f_{0,\star}^{(+)}(t)-f_{0,\star}^{(-)}(t)
 =-2a_{\circ,0}h_\circ K_T^{-1/2}\psi_\circ'(t).             \tag{7}
\]
They agree off \(\operatorname{supp}(\psi_\circ')\), and on that support
\(f_{0,\star}^{(-)}\ge c_f\).  The identity
\(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(f_+\|f_-)=\int f_+\log(f_+/f_-)\), the inequality
\(\log x\le x-1\), and \(\int(f_+-f_-)=0\) imply
\[
 D_{\mathrm{KL}}(f_+\|f_-)
 \le\int\frac{(f_+-f_-)^2}{f_-}.
\]
Patient independence and (7) consequently give
\[
 \begin{split}
 D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_+\|P_-)
 &\le K_T\int\frac{(f_{0,\star}^{(+)}-f_{0,\star}^{(-)})^2}
                         {f_{0,\star}^{(-)}}\,dt\\
 &\le\frac{4a_{\circ,0}^2h_\circ^2}{c_f}
       \int_0^{\bar\tau}\{\psi_\circ'(t)\}^2\,dt.           \tag{8}
 \end{split}
\]
Moreover,
\((\sqrt{x}-\sqrt y)^2\le(x-y)^2/y\) for \(x,y>0\).  Applying this
pointwise in (7), multiplying the Hellinger affinities of the independent
records, and using total variation bounded by the corresponding Hellinger
distance yields
\[
 \|P_+-P_-\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le2|a_{\circ,0}|h_\circ c_f^{-1/2}
       \left\{\int_0^{\bar\tau}(\psi_\circ')^2\right\}^{1/2}. \tag{9}
\]
The last inequality in the explicit compatibility assumption makes (9) a
fixed constant strictly below the amount required in the two-point width
argument.  Exact rank, spectrum, Gram, and normalization were established
in (1)--(4) and do not depend on the sign of the target loading. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
There is a constant \(c_{\mathrm{int}}=c_{\mathrm{int}}(L,\bar\tau,\beta)<\infty\) such that, for the piecewise-linear interpolant \(\widehat\theta_r\) in \(\mathrm{def:fpcr-multiplier-band}\),
\[
 0\le \|\widehat\theta_r-\theta\|_{\infty,\mathcal I}
 -\max_{g\in\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}}|\widehat\theta_r(g)-\theta(g)|
 \le c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{\min\{\beta+1,2\}}
\]
uniformly over \(\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\). Consequently the interpolation allowance under the corrected grid definition is \(O(\rho_r)\), so continuous-time honesty is not obtained by replacing \(\mathcal I\) with a fixed finite grid.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\), and set
\(q=\min\{\beta+1,2\}\).  By the hazard identity and endpoint
normalization,
\[
 \theta(t)=S^0_{1,\star}(t)
 =\exp\left\{-\int_0^t\lambda^0_{1,\star}(u)\,du\right\}.
\]
The bound \(\|\lambda^0_{1,\star}\|_{C^\beta(\mathcal I)}\le L\), the
fixed horizon, and the product H\"older inequality applied to
\(\theta'=-\lambda^0_{1,\star}\theta\) imply
\[
 \|\theta\|_{C^{\beta+1}(\mathcal I)}
 \le C(L,\bar\tau,\beta).                                   \tag{1}
\]
Let \(I_{\mathcal G}\theta\) be the piecewise-linear interpolant of the
grid values of \(\theta\).  On a grid interval \([a,b]\) of length at most
\(h=h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\), the first-order Taylor formula with H\"older
remainder when \(q<2\), and the ordinary second-order interpolation
remainder when \(q=2\), give
\[
 \sup_{t\in[a,b]}|I_{\mathcal G}\theta(t)-\theta(t)|
 \le C(L,\bar\tau,\beta)|b-a|^q.
\]
Taking the maximum over intervals yields
\[
 \|I_{\mathcal G}\theta-\theta\|_\infty
 \le c_{\mathrm{int}}h^q.                                  \tag{2}
\]

By construction, \(\widehat\theta_r\) is linear between adjacent grid
points.  Hence \(\widehat\theta_r-I_{\mathcal G}\theta\) is also linear
there, and the maximum of its absolute value is attained at an endpoint.
Consequently,
\[
 \|\widehat\theta_r-\theta\|_{\infty,\mathcal I}
 \le \max_{g\in\mathcal G}|\widehat\theta_r(g)-\theta(g)|
 +\|I_{\mathcal G}\theta-\theta\|_\infty.                  \tag{3}
\]
The reverse inequality between the grid maximum and the continuous
supremum follows from \(\mathcal G\subset\mathcal I\).  Combining (2)--(3)
proves the asserted two-sided interpolation inequality.  Finally, the mesh
condition in \(\mathrm{def:inference\mbox{-}grid}\) is \(h^q\le\rho_r\),
so the allowance is \(O(\rho_r)\). \(\square\)
statements.justification: The corrected exponent prices continuous-time interpolation at exactly the order supported by hazard smoothness and a linear interpolant.
statements.gap: HanShah2025SSC uses a finite evaluation grid and does not charge interpolation error to simultaneous coverage.
statements.consumer: It supports whole-trajectory clinical reporting once the stochastic band theorem is available.

statements.statement:
For each fixed \(r\ge1\), there is \(a_0<\infty\) such that, at every evaluated triple with \(\min\{N_0,K_T,K_D\}\ge a_0\), the band \(\widehat B_r\) belongs to \(\mathcal H_r(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)\). There is a constant \(c_{\mathrm{up}}<\infty\), independent of \(N_0\), \(K_T\), and \(K_D\), such that at every such triple,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)}E_P[w(\widehat B_r)]
 \le c_{\mathrm{up}}\bar\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D).
\]
Both assertions hold uniformly over every three-dimensional tail, with no balanced-growth or relative-rate restriction. In particular, \(\bar\rho_1=\rho_1=(N_0K_D)^{-1/2}\); for fixed \(r\ge2\), the displayed upper bound is \(O(\rho_r)\) on every subregime satisfying \(\eta_D(K_D)=O(\rho_r)\). No unrestricted higher-rank \(O(\rho_r)\) claim is made by this theorem.
statements.justification: This is the implementable honest patient-level replacement for the empirical donor bootstrap, with its exact estimator-specific width envelope.
statements.gap: HanShah2025SSC supplies finite-grid consistency and donor resampling, but not an interpolation-stable patient-martingale band with finite-tail coverage and a quantified total-estimator bias allowance.
statements.consumer: The PETAL Synthetic Survival Control analysis can report a valid simultaneous post-control survival band and its honest width guarantee.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Put \(\varepsilon=\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)\), and let \(Z_r\),
\(\mathfrak b_r\), and \(Q_r\) be the grid processes in
\(\mathrm{lem:uniform\mbox{-}linearization}\).  At every sufficiently large
triple, that lemma gives
\[
 \sup_P P\{\|Z_r\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}>c_r^\xi+\omega_r/2\}
 \le\alpha-\varepsilon/4,
 \qquad
 \sup_P P\{\|Q_r\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}>\omega_r/2\}
 \le\varepsilon/4,                                          \tag{1}
\]
and
\[
 \|\mathfrak b_r\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}
 \le\mathbf 1\{r\ge2\}\eta_D(K_D).                         \tag{2}
\]
A union bound in (1), followed by the gridwise expansion and (2), gives,
uniformly in \(P\),
\[
 P\!\left\{
 \max_{g\in\mathcal G}|\widehat\theta_r(g)-\theta(g)|
 \le c_r^\xi+\mathbf 1\{r\ge2\}\eta_D(K_D)+\omega_r
 \right\}\ge1-\alpha.                                       \tag{3}
\]
The equality between the interpolated population comparison and \(\theta\)
at the grid points, which is used in (3), follows only after the internal
\(L^2\) spectrum and Gram perturbations have been controlled.

Set \(q=\min\{\beta+1,2\}\).  By
\(\mathrm{prop:grid\mbox{-}interpolation}\),
\[
 \|\widehat\theta_r-\theta\|_{\infty,\mathcal I}
 \le\max_{g\in\mathcal G}|\widehat\theta_r(g)-\theta(g)|
 +c_{\mathrm{int}}h^q,
 \qquad h^q\le\rho_r.                                      \tag{4}
\]
Projection onto \([0,1]\) cannot increase distance from
\(\theta(g)\in[0,1]\).  Linear interpolation of the projected grid values
has its largest deviation from the linear interpolant of \(\theta\) at a
grid endpoint, and \(\theta(0)=1\).  The radius \(A_r\) in
\(\mathrm{def:fpcr\mbox{-}multiplier\mbox{-}band}\) is exactly the right
side of (3) plus the final term in (4).  Hence (3)--(4) imply
\[
 P\{\widehat B_r^{\mathrm{lo}}(t)\le\theta(t)\le
       \widehat B_r^{\mathrm{up}}(t)
       \text{ for every }t\in\mathcal I\}\ge1-\alpha.       \tag{5}
\]
This is stronger than \(1-\alpha-\varepsilon\), so
\(\widehat B_r\in\mathcal H_r(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)\).

Clipping the endpoints to \([0,1]\) can only reduce width.  Therefore
\[
 w(\widehat B_r)
 \le2c_r^\xi+2\mathbf 1\{r\ge2\}\eta_D(K_D)
      +2\omega_r+2c_{\mathrm{int}}h^q.                     \tag{6}
\]
For all sufficiently large triples,
\(q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\le1-\alpha/2\).  Conditional on the data, let
\(Z_r^\xi\) denote the multiplier linear process whose quantile is
\(c_r^\xi\).  The bounded martingale integrands and the dyadic-net
calculation in the proof of the linearization lemma give
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_r}E_P E_\xi
       \|Z_r^\xi\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}^2\le C\rho_r^2.       \tag{7}
\]
Conditional Markov inequality at tail probability at least \(\alpha/2\)
gives
\[
 c_r^\xi\le (2/\alpha)^{1/2}
       \{E_\xi\|Z_r^\xi\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}^2\}^{1/2}.
\]
Jensen's inequality and (7) yield
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_r}E_Pc_r^\xi\le C\rho_r.             \tag{8}
\]
Also \(h^q\le\rho_r\), and the channel-by-channel calculation in the
linearization lemma gives \(\omega_r=o(\rho_r)\) uniformly on every
three-dimensional tail.  Taking expectations in (6), using (8), and
increasing the common lower-tail cutoff \(a_0\) if necessary proves
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_r}E_Pw(\widehat B_r)
 \le C\{\rho_r+\mathbf 1\{r\ge2\}\eta_D(K_D)\}
 =C\bar\rho_r.                                               \tag{9}
\]
At \(r=1\), the risk-exhaustion term is absent by definition, so
\(\bar\rho_1=\rho_1=(N_0K_D)^{-1/2}\).  If \(r\ge2\) and
\(\eta_D(K_D)=O(\rho_r)\), then \(\bar\rho_r=O(\rho_r)\).
No step compares the relative growth of \(K_T\), \(N_0\), and \(K_D\), so
(5) and (9) are uniform on every three-dimensional tail. \(\square\)

statements.statement: There are constants \(a_0<\infty\) and \(c_{\mathrm{low}}>0\) such that, at every evaluated triple with \(\min\{N_0,K_T,K_D\}\ge a_0\), every \(B\in\mathcal H_1(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)\) satisfies \[\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_1(N_0,K_T,K_D)}E_P[w(B)]\ge c_{\mathrm{low}}(N_0K_D)^{-1/2},\] and, for every fixed \(r\ge2\), every \(B\in\mathcal H_r(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)\) satisfies \[\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)}E_P[w(B)]\ge c_{\mathrm{low}}\{K_T^{-1/2}+(N_0K_D)^{-1/2}\}.\] The donor channel uses a normalization-preserving post-donor hazard pair of size \((N_0K_D)^{-1/2}\). The target channel embeds the explicit rank-two pair from \(\mathrm{lem:rank-two-pair}\) and adds fixed orthogonal contrast directions for \(r>2\). All pairs preserve valid survival laws, endpoint normalization, exact primitive rank, the nonzero contrast-spectrum and pre-contrast Gram bounds, and uniformly bounded total variation.
statements.justification: The two explicit normalization-preserving pairs certify the unavoidable donor and target-pre channels.
statements.gap: Existing scalar synthetic-control decompositions do not supply these exact-rank survival-law converses.
statements.consumer: The lower bound prevents reporting a donor-only band when loading uncertainty is unavoidable.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Put \(n_D=N_0K_D\).  We first construct the donor channel.  Keep the
centered polynomial donor scores, all factor curves, all pre-period laws,
and target loading zero fixed, and replace only the post baseline by
\[
 s_1^{(u)}(t)=e^{-\lambda_\circ t}
              +u c n_D^{-1/2}\psi_\circ(t),
 \qquad u\in\{-1,+1\}.                                      \tag{1}
\]
Choose the fixed \(c>0\) sufficiently small as specified below.  For every
sufficiently large triple, \(cn_D^{-1/2}\le v_\circ\).  The pointwise
inequalities in
\(\mathrm{ass:explicit\mbox{-}witness\mbox{-}compatibility}\) verify
survival validity, event overlap, the failure-density floor, and hazard
smoothness.  Adding a common post-period curve does not alter the centered
donor operator, so exact rank and its nonzero singular values are unchanged.
The pre-factor Gram, loading bounds, factor envelope, and endpoint
normalization are likewise unchanged.  With censoring identically infinite,
the censoring, consistency, and sampling conditions hold.

The two donor-channel laws differ only in the \(n_D\) donor-post records,
and their target curves have separation
\[
 \Delta_D=2c\|\psi_\circ\|_\infty n_D^{-1/2}.                \tag{2}
\]
For a donor-post record, the density difference is
\(-2cn_D^{-1/2}\psi_\circ'\).  The density floor on the support of this
difference and the same calculation as in
\(\mathrm{lem:rank\mbox{-}two\mbox{-}pair}\) give
\[
 D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q_{D,+}\|Q_{D,-})
 \le 4c^2c_f^{-1}\int_0^{\bar\tau}(\psi_\circ')^2,
 \qquad
 \|Q_{D,+}-Q_{D,-}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le C_Dc.                 \tag{3}
\]
Choose \(c\) so that the last quantity is at most
\(\frac34(1/2-\alpha)\).  This construction applies at rank one under the
zero-dimensional convention and at every fixed higher rank using the fixed
orthogonal backbone from
\(\mathrm{def:rank\mbox{-}two\mbox{-}lecam\mbox{-}pair}\).

For the target channel at rank \(r\ge2\), use \(P_{r,+}\) and \(P_{r,-}\)
from that fixed-rank construction.  Centering and empirical
Gram--Schmidt give
\[
 N_0^{-1}\sum_mz_m=0,
 \qquad
 N_0^{-1}\sum_mz_mz_m^\top=I_d.                             \tag{4}
\]
The joint-period factor columns are orthogonal with common squared norm
\((a_{\circ,0}^2+a_{\circ,1}^2)\|\psi_\circ\|_2^2\), so the centered
operator has exactly \(d=r-1\) nonzero singular values, all in the
permitted interval.  Similarly,
\[
 \int_{\mathcal I}A_{0,d}(t)A_{0,d}(t)^\top\,dt
 =a_{\circ,0}^2\|\psi_\circ\|_2^2 I_d.                      \tag{5}
\]
The row bound in the compatibility assumption gives donor incoherence.
Since \(M_\star>0\), eventually
\[
 h_\circ K_T^{-1/2}\le\min\{M_\star,R_d\}.                  \tag{6}
\]
The remaining class properties follow from the explicit compatibility
inequalities.  Only the first target-loading coordinate changes, so
\[
 \Delta_T
 =2|a_{\circ,1}|h_\circ\|\psi_\circ\|_\infty K_T^{-1/2},    \tag{7}
\]
and the target-pair lemma gives
\[
 \|P_{r,+}-P_{r,-}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le2|a_{\circ,0}|h_\circ c_f^{-1/2}\|\psi_\circ'\|_2
 \le\frac34(1/2-\alpha).                                    \tag{8}
\]
Equations (4)--(6) show explicitly that the added orthogonal directions for
\(r>2\) preserve endpoint normalization, exact primitive rank, spectrum,
and pre-contrast Gram bounds.

We now convert either pair into a width bound.  Let \(Q_-,Q_+\) be one of
the two pairs, let \(\theta_-,\theta_+\) be its targets, and set
\[
 \zeta=\alpha+\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha).
\]
For \(u\in\{-,+\}\), honesty of \(B\) under \(Q_u\) gives
\[
 Q_u\{\theta_u(t)\in B(t)\text{ for every }t\in\mathcal I\}
 \ge1-\zeta.                                                 \tag{9}
\]
Transfer the \(+\) event from \(Q_+\) to \(Q_-\) by total variation and
intersect it with the \(-\) event in (9).  This gives
\[
 Q_-\{\theta_-,\theta_+\in B\}
 \ge1-2\zeta-\|Q_--Q_+\|_{\mathrm{TV}}.                     \tag{10}
\]
On the event in (10), at a time maximizing
\(|\theta_+-\theta_-|\), one has
\[
 w(B)\ge\|\theta_+-\theta_-\|_\infty.                       \tag{11}
\]
The coverage schedule satisfies
\[
 \varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)
 \le\frac14(1/2-\alpha),
 \qquad
 1-2\zeta\ge\frac32(1/2-\alpha).                            \tag{12}
\]
Equations (3), (8), (10), and (12) therefore make the probability in
(10) at least \(\frac34(1/2-\alpha)>0\) for both channels.  Taking
expectations in (11) and using (2) and (7) yields constants
\(c_D,c_T>0\), depending only on the fixed model constants and \(\alpha\),
such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_r}E_Pw(B)\ge c_Dn_D^{-1/2},          \tag{13}
\]
and, when \(r\ge2\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_r}E_Pw(B)\ge c_TK_T^{-1/2}.          \tag{14}
\]
For \(r=1\), (13) is the asserted bound.  For \(r\ge2\), use
\(\max\{a,b\}\ge(a+b)/2\) in (13)--(14), and decrease the constant, to
obtain the asserted sum.  All membership and total-variation bounds hold
at every sufficiently large evaluated triple and do not impose a
relative-growth condition. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
For fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\) and every fixed exact rank \(r\), there are \(a_0<\infty\) and constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that, uniformly over every evaluated triple with \(\min\{N_0,K_T,K_D\}\ge a_0\), without relative-growth restrictions,
\[
 W_1^*(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)\asymp(N_0K_D)^{-1/2},
\]
and, for \(r\ge2\),
\[
 c\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)
 \le W_r^*(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)
 \le C\bar\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D).
\]
Consequently \(W_r^*(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)\asymp\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\) on every subregime satisfying \(\eta_D(K_D)=O(\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D))\).  Without that subregime condition, the displayed bracket is the proved unrestricted conclusion and its tightness is not asserted.  Each infimum is over bands satisfying the coverage constraint at that same evaluated triple.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Fix \(r\) and a sufficiently large evaluated triple.  By
\(\mathrm{thm:normalization\mbox{-}preserving\mbox{-}converse}\), every
admissible band has maximal expected width at least \(c\rho_r\).  Taking
the infimum over the same per-triple honesty class in
\(\mathrm{def:minimax\mbox{-}width}\) gives
\[
 W_r^*(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)\ge c\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D).         \tag{1}
\]
By \(\mathrm{thm:attaining\mbox{-}band}\), the explicit band
\(\widehat B_r\) is in that honesty class and obeys
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_r}E_Pw(\widehat B_r)
 \le C\bar\rho_r.                                           \tag{2}
\]
Using \(\widehat B_r\) as a single data-dependent witness in the minimax
infimum yields
\[
 W_r^*(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)\le C\bar\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D).     \tag{3}
\]
At rank one,
\(\bar\rho_1=\rho_1=(N_0K_D)^{-1/2}\), so (1)--(3) prove
\[
 W_1^*(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)\asymp(N_0K_D)^{-1/2}.            \tag{4}
\]
For fixed \(r\ge2\), (1)--(3) give the unrestricted bracket
\[
 c\{K_T^{-1/2}+(N_0K_D)^{-1/2}\}
 \le W_r^*(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)
 \le C\{K_T^{-1/2}+(N_0K_D)^{-1/2}+\eta_D(K_D)\}.           \tag{5}
\]
Whenever \(\eta_D(K_D)=O(\rho_r)\), the two sides of (5) match and hence
\(W_r^*\asymp\rho_r\).  The constants and the common lower-tail cutoff are
uniform over every three-dimensional tail because the two input theorems
have that property.  No comparison among the relative growth rates has
been introduced.  The infimum on each line is the per-triple infimum from
\(\mathrm{def:minimax\mbox{-}width}\). \(\square\)
statements.justification: This is the exact rank-normalization transition at rank one and the honest unrestricted higher-rank minimax bracket delivered by the current total estimator and converse.
statements.gap: No located synthetic-control, survival-band, or low-rank inference paper gives the donor-only rank-one frontier or this explicit two-channel higher-rank bracket with its risk-exhaustion term.
statements.consumer: It tells trial and registry designers when the two-channel rate is matched and displays the precise residual width term outside that subregime.

statements.statement: On the homogeneous normalized special case \(r=1\), \(\widehat\theta_1\) and \(\widehat B_1\) reduce, up to the stated interpolation allowance, to the pooled donor-post Kaplan--Meier estimator and its patient-level martingale-multiplier simultaneous band based on \(N_0K_D\) observations.
statements.justification: The reduction is the required sanity check against classical one-sample survival-band theory.
statements.gap: DoblerPaulyScheike2019 validates martingale bands for survival functionals but does not derive this normalized Synthetic Survival Control reduction.
statements.consumer: It supplies a transparent implementation check for the rank-one software path.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
At \(r=1\), \(d=0\).  By
\(\mathrm{lem:normalization\mbox{-}collapse}\), every factor and loading
product is an empty sum and no target-pre record enters either the causal
target or the estimator.  The estimator definition therefore sets
\(\widehat\theta_1\) exactly equal to the Kaplan--Meier curve formed by
pooling the \(N_0K_D\) donor-post patients.  Its empirical derivative is
the ordinary pooled product-limit martingale derivative.  Attaching one
independent multiplier to each patient consequently gives exactly the
patient-level simultaneous multiplier process in the rank-one branch.

The correction \(\mathbf 1\{r\ge2\}\eta_D(K_D)\) vanishes, and
\(\mathrm{lem:uniform\mbox{-}linearization}\) gives
\(\omega_1=o((N_0K_D)^{-1/2})\).  Finally,
\(\mathrm{prop:grid\mbox{-}interpolation}\) supplies the stated
continuous-time interpolation allowance, and
\(\mathrm{thm:attaining\mbox{-}band}\) supplies its simultaneous honesty.
Thus the rank-one branch is precisely the pooled donor-post patient-level
Kaplan--Meier martingale-multiplier construction asserted in the
proposition. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
For an observed control cell with \(k\) patients and \(k\) large enough, let \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\) be the deterministic piecewise-linear interpolation operator on \(\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\), and set \(\widetilde S^0_{p,m}=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}S^0_{p,m}\).  Its linearly interpolated Kaplan--Meier curve admits the uniform decomposition
\[
 \widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{p,m}-\widetilde S^0_{p,m}
 =k^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{k}\varphi_{p,m,j}+b_{p,m,k}+q_{p,m,k}
 \quad\hbox{in }\ell^\infty(\mathcal I),
\]
where the \(\varphi_{p,m,j}\) are independent, mean-zero censoring-martingale influence processes, \(\|b_{p,m,k}\|_\infty\le C_0e^{-c_0k}\), \(E q_{p,m,k}=0\), and \(E\|q_{p,m,k}\|_\infty^2\le C_0k^{-2}\), uniformly over the model class.  Here \(c_0=s_-g_-/3\), and \(C_0\) may be chosen as the conservative fixed constant used in the definition of \(\eta_D\).  Moreover, with \(q_\beta=\min\{\beta+1,2\}\),
\[
 \widetilde S^0_{p,m}(g)=S^0_{p,m}(g)\quad(g\in\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}),
 \qquad
 \|\widetilde S^0_{p,m}-S^0_{p,m}\|_\infty
 \le c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q_\beta},
\]
and
\[
 \|\widetilde S^0_{p,m}-S^0_{p,m}\|_{L^2(\mathcal I)}
 \le \bar\tau^{1/2}c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q_\beta},
\]
where \(c_{\mathrm{int}}=c_{\mathrm{int}}(L,\bar\tau,\beta)<\infty\).  Thus the exact expansion about \(S^0_{p,m}\) contains the additional deterministic term \(a_{\mathcal G,p,m}=\widetilde S^0_{p,m}-S^0_{p,m}\), which is zero on the grid and is controlled only by the displayed interpolation bounds.  For independent donor cells, averaging the \(q_{p,m,k}\) terms has order \(O_P(N_0^{-1/2}k^{-1})=o_P((N_0k)^{-1/2})\), whereas averaging the bias or interpolation terms need not improve their respective uniform bounds.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Fix one observed control cell and suppress its \((p,m)\) subscripts until the donor-averaging step.  Let \(\widehat S^{\mathrm{PL}}\) denote the un-interpolated product-limit step curve.  For \(1\le j\le k\), define
\[
 N_j(u)=\mathbf 1\{X_j\le u,\Delta_j=1\},\qquad
 Y_j(u)=\mathbf 1\{X_j\ge u\},\qquad
 Y(u)=\sum_{j=1}^kY_j(u),
\]
using the predictable left-continuous version of the at-risk process at jump times.  Independent censoring implies that the compensator of \(N_j\) is
\[
 \int_0^uY_j(v)\lambda^0(v)\,dv.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 M_j(u)=N_j(u)-\int_0^uY_j(v)\lambda^0(v)\,dv
\]
is a mean-zero square-integrable martingale.  Patient independence makes these martingales independent.  Put
\[
 M=\sum_{j=1}^kM_j,\qquad
 J(u)=\mathbf 1\{Y(u)>0\},\qquad
 H(u)=E Y_j(u)=S^0(u)G(u).
\]
The last equality uses independent censoring and continuity of the event-time law induced by its hazard.  Censoring and event overlap give
\[
 H(u)\ge h_0:=s_-g_->0,
 \qquad u\in\mathcal I.                                      \tag{1}
\]
Hazard smoothness gives
\[
 \sup_{u\in\mathcal I}\lambda^0(u)\le L,
 \qquad
 \Lambda^0(\bar\tau):=\int_0^{\bar\tau}\lambda^0(u)\,du
 \le L\bar\tau.                                               \tag{2}
\]

Set \(R=\widehat S^{\mathrm{PL}}/S^0\).  The product-integral equations are
\[
 d\widehat S^{\mathrm{PL}}(u)
 =-\widehat S^{\mathrm{PL}}(u-)\frac{J(u)}{Y(u)}\,dN(u),
 \qquad
 dS^0(u)=-S^0(u)\lambda^0(u)\,du,
\]
where \(J/Y\) is defined to be zero when the risk set is empty.  Integration by parts and \(dN=dM+Y\lambda^0du\) give the exact identity
\[
 R(t)-1
 =-\int_0^tR(u-)\frac{J(u)}{Y(u)}\,dM(u)
  +\int_0^tR(u-)\{1-J(u)\}\lambda^0(u)\,du.                 \tag{3}
\]
Thus the identity never divides by zero.  Moreover, event overlap and \(0\le\widehat S^{\mathrm{PL}}\le1\) imply
\[
 0\le R(u)\le s_-^{-1}.                                      \tag{4}
\]

Define the un-interpolated influence process
\[
 \varphi_j^{\mathrm{PL}}(t)
 =-S^0(t)\int_0^tH(u)^{-1}\,dM_j(u).                         \tag{5}
\]
Its deterministic integrand is bounded by \(h_0^{-1}\), so the \(\varphi_j^{\mathrm{PL}}\) are independent and mean zero.  Subtracting \(k^{-1}\sum_j\varphi_j^{\mathrm{PL}}\) from (3), after multiplication by \(S^0(t)\), yields
\[
 \widehat S^{\mathrm{PL}}(t)-S^0(t)
 -k^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^k\varphi_j^{\mathrm{PL}}(t)
 =V_k(t)+A_k(t),                                               \tag{6}
\]
where
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 V_k(t)&=-S^0(t)\int_0^tD_k(u)\,dM(u),\\
 D_k(u)&=R(u-)\frac{J(u)}{Y(u)}-\frac{1}{kH(u)},\\
 A_k(t)&=S^0(t)\int_0^tR(u-)\{1-J(u)\}\lambda^0(u)\,du.
 \end{aligned}                                                 \tag{7}
\]
All integrands in (5) and (7) are predictable.

We first isolate the exponentially small risk-exhaustion bias.  The stochastic integral defining \(V_k\) is integrable and has expectation zero.  Since the risk indicators are nonincreasing, \(A_k\) can be nonzero only on
\[
 \mathcal X_k=\{Y(\bar\tau)=0\}.
\]
Patient independence and (1) imply
\[
 \Pr(\mathcal X_k)=\{1-H(\bar\tau)\}^k
 \le e^{-kH(\bar\tau)}\le e^{-h_0k}.                         \tag{8}
\]
By (2), (4), and Fubini's theorem,
\[
 \|EA_k\|_\infty
 \le s_-^{-1}L\bar\tau e^{-h_0k}.                            \tag{9}
\]
Set
\[
 b_k^{\mathrm{PL}}=EA_k,
 \qquad
 q_k^{\mathrm{PL}}=V_k+A_k-EA_k.                             \tag{10}
\]
Equations (6) and (10) give the desired step-curve decomposition, and \(Eq_k^{\mathrm{PL}}=0\).  Since \(c_0=h_0/3<h_0\), a fixed enlargement of the constant gives
\[
 \|b_k^{\mathrm{PL}}\|_\infty\le C_0e^{-c_0k}.             \tag{11}
\]

We next bound the second-order remainder.  Let
\[
 \mathcal E_k=\{Y(\bar\tau)\ge kh_0/2\}.
\]
The variable \(Y(\bar\tau)\) is binomial with success probability at least \(h_0\).  The Chernoff bound, obtained by applying exponential Markov inequality to \(e^{-sY(\bar\tau)}\) and optimizing over \(s>0\), therefore gives
\[
 \Pr(\mathcal E_k^c)\le e^{-c_1k}                            \tag{12}
\]
for a fixed \(c_1=c_1(h_0)>0\).  On \(\mathcal E_k\), monotonicity gives \(Y(u)\ge kh_0/2\) and \(J(u)=1\) throughout \(\mathcal I\), and hence
\[
 D_k(u)=\frac{R(u-)-1}{Y(u)}
 -\frac{Y(u)-kH(u)}{kH(u)Y(u)}.                              \tag{13}
\]

Stop (3) the first time that the risk set falls below \(kh_0/2\).  Before this time the exhaustion term is zero, and the predictable quadratic variation of the stopped stochastic integral is bounded, by (2) and (4), as
\[
 \int_0^{\bar\tau}R(u-)^2\frac{J(u)}{Y(u)}\lambda^0(u)\,du
 \le Ck^{-1}.                                                 \tag{14}
\]
The square-integrable martingale maximal inequality gives \(E\sup_{u\le\bar\tau}|U(u)|^2\le4E\langle U\rangle(\bar\tau)\).  On \(\mathcal E_k\) the stopping time exceeds \(\bar\tau\), so (14) yields
\[
 E\bigl[\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_k}\|R-1\|_\infty^2\bigr]
 \le Ck^{-1}.                                                 \tag{15}
\]
For every fixed \(u\), patient independence gives
\[
 E\{Y(u)-kH(u)\}^2=kH(u)\{1-H(u)\}\le k.                  \tag{16}
\]
Using (13), \(Y\ge kh_0/2\), (2), (15), and (16), we obtain
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E\left[\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_k}
   \int_0^{\bar\tau}D_k(u)^2Y(u)\lambda^0(u)\,du\right]
 &\le \frac{C}{k}E\bigl[\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_k}\|R-1\|_\infty^2\bigr]\\
 &\quad+\frac{C}{k^3}\int_0^{\bar\tau}
       E\{Y(u)-kH(u)\}^2\lambda^0(u)\,du\\
 &\le Ck^{-2}.
 \end{aligned}                                                 \tag{17}
\]
On \(\mathcal E_k^c\), (1), (2), and (4) yield the pointwise bound
\[
 D_k(u)^2Y(u)
 \le 2s_-^{-2}\frac{J(u)}{Y(u)}+\frac{2Y(u)}{k^2h_0^2}
 \le C.
\]
Consequently, (12) implies
\[
 E\left[\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_k^c}
   \int_0^{\bar\tau}D_k(u)^2Y(u)\lambda^0(u)\,du\right]
 \le Ce^{-c_1k}\le Ck^{-2}.                                 \tag{18}
\]
The martingale maximal inequality and (17)--(18) show
\[
 E\|V_k\|_\infty^2\le Ck^{-2}.                              \tag{19}
\]
The process \(A_k\) vanishes off \(\mathcal X_k\), and (2)--(4) bound its supremum norm by a fixed constant.  Thus (8) gives
\[
 E\|A_k-EA_k\|_\infty^2\le Ce^{-h_0k}\le Ck^{-2}.           \tag{20}
\]
Combining (10), (19), and (20), and enlarging \(C_0\) once more, proves
\[
 E\|q_k^{\mathrm{PL}}\|_\infty^2\le C_0k^{-2}.             \tag{21}
\]
Every constant through (21) depends only on the fixed overlap, hazard, and horizon bounds, so the estimates are uniform over the exact-rank model class.

We now prove the asserted cross-donor rate in supremum norm.  Restore the donor index and write
\[
 U_m(t)=\int_0^tD_{m,k}(u)\,dM_m(u),
 \qquad
 V_{m,k}(t)=-S_m^0(t)U_m(t).
\]
The calculation in (17)--(18) gives, uniformly in \(m\),
\[
 E\int_0^{\bar\tau}D_{m,k}(u)^2Y_m(u)\lambda_m^0(u)\,du
 \le Ck^{-2}.                                                   \tag{22}
\]
Integration by parts gives
\[
 \sum_{m\in\mathcal D}S_m^0(t)U_m(t)
 =\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\int_0^tS_m^0(u)\,dU_m(u)
  +\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\int_0^tU_m(u)\,dS_m^0(u).          \tag{23}
\]
The first term on the right is a martingale.  Independence of donor cells makes all cross predictable covariations zero, so (22) and the maximal inequality bound its expected squared supremum by \(CN_0k^{-2}\).  For the second term, use \(dS_m^0(u)=-S_m^0(u)\lambda_m^0(u)du\), Cauchy--Schwarz in \(u\), and independence together with \(EU_m(u)=0\):
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E\sup_{t\in\mathcal I}
 \left|\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\int_0^tU_m(u)\,dS_m^0(u)\right|^2
 &\le \bar\tau\int_0^{\bar\tau}
 E\left|\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}S_m^0(u)\lambda_m^0(u)U_m(u)\right|^2du\\
 &=\bar\tau\int_0^{\bar\tau}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}
 S_m^0(u)^2\lambda_m^0(u)^2EU_m(u)^2du\\
 &\le CN_0k^{-2}.
 \end{aligned}                                                 \tag{24}
\]
After division by \(N_0^2\), (23)--(24) prove
\[
 E\left\|N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}V_{m,k}\right\|_\infty^2
 \le \frac{C}{N_0k^2}.                                      \tag{25}
\]

The centered exhaustion processes have the same donor rate.  Each \(A_{m,k}\) vanishes unless \(\mathcal X_{m,k}\) occurs.  Differentiating (7) away from its exhaustion time gives
\[
 A_{m,k}'(t)=-\lambda_m^0(t)A_{m,k}(t)
 +\widehat S_m^{\mathrm{PL}}(t)\{1-J_m(t)\}\lambda_m^0(t).
\]
Thus \(A_{m,k}(0)=0\) and
\[
 |A_{m,k}(t)-A_{m,k}(s)|
 \le C|t-s|\mathbf 1_{\mathcal X_{m,k}},
 \qquad
 \Pr(\mathcal X_{m,k})\le e^{-h_0k}.                        \tag{26}
\]
For completeness, condition on the \(A_{m,k}\)'s and symmetrize by independent Rademacher signs \(\epsilon_m\).  On a dyadic partition of \(\mathcal I\) at level \(\ell\), (26) makes every normalized signed adjacent increment sub-Gaussian with variance proxy at most
\[
 C2^{-2\ell}N_0^{-2}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}
 \mathbf 1_{\mathcal X_{m,k}}.
\]
Exponential Markov inequality and a union bound over at most \(2^{\ell+1}\) increments bound the conditional expected maximum at level \(\ell\) by a constant times
\[
 2^{-\ell}\sqrt{\ell+1}\,
 N_0^{-1}\left(\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}
 \mathbf 1_{\mathcal X_{m,k}}\right)^{1/2}.
\]
The sum over \(\ell\) is finite; integrating the same sub-Gaussian tail gives the corresponding squared bound.  Ghost-sample symmetrization and (26) therefore yield
\[
 E\left\|N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}
 \{A_{m,k}-EA_{m,k}\}\right\|_\infty^2
 \le \frac{C}{N_0^2}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}
 \Pr(\mathcal X_{m,k})
 \le \frac{Ce^{-h_0k}}{N_0}
 \le \frac{C}{N_0k^2}.                                      \tag{27}
\]
Combining (10), (25), and (27) proves
\[
 E\left\|N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}q_{m,k}^{\mathrm{PL}}
 \right\|_\infty^2
 \le \frac{C}{N_0k^2}.                                      \tag{28}
\]

It remains to transfer the decomposition to the interpolated estimator without absorbing interpolation error into the Kaplan--Meier bias.  Let \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\) denote the deterministic piecewise-linear interpolation operator on the common grid, and define
\[
 \widetilde S^0=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}S^0,
 \qquad
 \varphi_j=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\varphi_j^{\mathrm{PL}},
 \qquad
 b_k=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}b_k^{\mathrm{PL}},
 \qquad
 q_k=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}q_k^{\mathrm{PL}}.
\]
The operator \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\) is linear, deterministic, and a contraction in supremum norm.  Since the construction defines \(\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\widehat S^{\mathrm{PL}}\), applying it to (6) gives the exact, correctly centered identity
\[
 \widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}-\widetilde S^0
 =k^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^k\varphi_j+b_k+q_k.                       \tag{29}
\]
The operator preserves expectations and patient independence, does not increase the bounds in (11), (21), or (28), and commutes with donor averaging because all cells use the same deterministic grid.  This proves every stochastic assertion in the corrected statement.

We finally quantify the deterministic difference between the true and interpolated population curves.  The hazard equation
\[
 (S^0)'=-\lambda^0S^0
\]
and the uniform \(C^\beta\) bound on \(\lambda^0\) imply a uniform \(C^{\beta+1}\) bound on \(S^0\).  Put \(\nu=\min\{\beta,1\}\).  On a grid interval \([g_0,g_1]\) of length at most the mesh, write \(t=g_0+u(g_1-g_0)\), where \(0\le u\le1\).  Cancellation of the constant derivative term gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 (\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}S^0)(t)-S^0(t)
 &=u\int_{g_0}^{g_1}\{(S^0)'(v)-(S^0)'(t)\}\,dv\\
 &\quad-\int_{g_0}^{t}\{(S^0)'(v)-(S^0)'(t)\}\,dv.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The \(C^\nu\) modulus of \((S^0)'\) therefore yields, with \(q_\beta=1+\nu=\min\{\beta+1,2\}\),
\[
 \|\widetilde S^0-S^0\|_\infty
 \le c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q_\beta}.              \tag{30}
\]
The interpolation operator reproduces endpoint values, so
\[
 \widetilde S^0(g)=S^0(g)
 \quad\text{for every }g\in\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}.         \tag{31}
\]
Integrating the squared pointwise bound in (30) over an interval of length \(\bar\tau\) gives
\[
 \|\widetilde S^0-S^0\|_{L^2(\mathcal I)}
 \le \bar\tau^{1/2}c_{\mathrm{int}}
 h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q_\beta}.                                  \tag{32}
\]
Thus, with \(a_{\mathcal G}=\widetilde S^0-S^0\), the expansion about the original population curve is exactly
\[
 \widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}-S^0
 =k^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^k\varphi_j+b_k+q_k+a_{\mathcal G},        \tag{33}
\]
where (30)--(32), rather than the exponential bias bound, control \(a_{\mathcal G}\).  In particular, \(a_{\mathcal G}\) generally does not vanish inside the internal \(L^2\) factor map even though it vanishes at every grid point.

By (28), contraction, and Markov's inequality,
\[
 \left\|N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}q_{p,m,k}\right\|_\infty
 =O_P(N_0^{-1/2}k^{-1}).                                    \tag{34}
\]
Dividing (34) by \((N_0k)^{-1/2}\) gives \(k^{-1/2}\to0\).  No assumption supplies cross-donor cancellation for either the deterministic biases or the interpolation remainders, so their averages retain the respective bounds in (11) and (30).  Finally, for the deterministic odd--even split in the functional-PCR construction, the smaller fold has \(\lfloor K_D/2\rfloor\) patients; substituting this value into (11) gives \(C_0\exp\{-c_0\lfloor K_D/2\rfloor\}\).  Since all preceding constants are fixed and uniform, \(C_0\) may be enlarged to the conservative constant used in \(\eta_D\).  This completes the proof. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Let \(q_\beta=\min\{\beta+1,2\}\), let \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\) be piecewise-linear interpolation on \(\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\), and define \(\widetilde S^0\), \(\widetilde s\), \(\widetilde Y_m\), and \(\widetilde\Gamma\) as in \(\mathrm{def:fpcr\mbox{-}multiplier\mbox{-}band}\). Put \(Y_m=(S^0_{0,m}-s_0,S^0_{1,m}-s_1)\) and \(\Gamma=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}Y_m\otimes Y_m\). There is a constant \(C_*<\infty\), depending only on the fixed model constants and \(r\), such that
\[
 \widetilde S^0_{p,m}(g)=S^0_{p,m}(g)\quad(g\in\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}),
 \qquad
 \max_{p,m}\|\widetilde S^0_{p,m}-S^0_{p,m}\|_\infty
 \le C_*h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q_\beta},
\]
and
\[
 \|\widetilde\Gamma-\Gamma\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le C_*h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q_\beta}.
\]
When \(d>0\), for every sufficiently fine grid the operator \(\widetilde\Gamma\) has exactly \(d\) positive eigenvalues, its \(d\)-th eigenvalue is at least \(\gamma_-^2/2\), and its selected projector \(\widetilde\Pi\) satisfies
\[
 \|\widetilde\Pi-\Pi\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le C_*h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q_\beta}.
\]
If \(\widetilde b_p\) denotes any selected positive-square-root factor coordinates of \(\widetilde\Gamma\), there is an orthogonal matrix \(R_{\mathcal G}\) such that
\[
 \max_{p\in\{0,1\}}\|\widetilde b_p-R_{\mathcal G}^{\top}b_p\|_{L^2}
 \le C_*h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q_\beta}.
\]
Consequently, with \(H_0=\int_{\mathcal I}b_0b_0^\top\) and \(\widetilde H_0=\int_{\mathcal I}\widetilde b_0\widetilde b_0^\top\),
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(\widetilde H_0)\ge\kappa_-/2,
 \qquad
 \|\widetilde H_0^{-1}-R_{\mathcal G}^{\top}H_0^{-1}R_{\mathcal G}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le C_*h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q_\beta}.
\]
The population comparison curve is exact for the interpolated panel:
\[
 \theta^{\mathrm{pop}}_{r,\mathcal G}=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\theta
 \quad\hbox{on }\mathcal I,
 \qquad
 \theta^{\mathrm{pop}}_{r,\mathcal G}(g)=\theta(g)
 \quad(g\in\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D});
\]
and for \(d=0\), the factor, projector, and Gram assertions use the zero-dimensional convention and the last display holds with \(\theta^{\mathrm{pop}}_{1,\mathcal G}=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}s_1\).
statements.justification: This lemma closes the internal interpolation gap by stabilizing the population factor map before differentiation.
statements.gap: The existing grid proposition controls only output interpolation; it does not control the covariance operator and pre-period inverse computed from interpolated curves.
statements.consumer: The gridwise functional-PCR expansion is centered at this stable interpolated population map.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\), write
\(h=h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\), and put
\(q_\beta=\min\{\beta+1,2\}\).  The hazard identity and endpoint
normalization give
\[
 S^0_{p,m}(t)
 =\exp\left\{-\int_0^t\lambda^0_{p,m}(u)\,du\right\}.        \tag{1}
\]
By \(\mathrm{ass:hazard\mbox{-}smoothness}\), the product rule applied to
\((S^0_{p,m})'=-\lambda^0_{p,m}S^0_{p,m}\) gives a uniform
\(C^{\beta+1}\) bound on every cell survival curve.  The piecewise-linear
interpolation remainder on each grid interval is therefore bounded by
\(C_*h^{q_\beta}\).  Interpolation reproduces its input at every knot, so
\[
 \widetilde S^0_{p,m}(g)=S^0_{p,m}(g),
 \qquad
 \|\widetilde S^0_{p,m}-S^0_{p,m}\|_\infty
 \le C_*h^{q_\beta}.                                        \tag{2}
\]
Because averaging and centering are linear and every cell uses the same
grid,
\[
 \widetilde s_p=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}s_p,
 \qquad
 \widetilde Y_m=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}Y_m.                 \tag{3}
\]
The donor incoherence and factor envelope assumptions give
\(\sup_m\|Y_m\|_{L^2}\le C\).  Equations (2)--(3), the fixed horizon, and
the triangle inequality give
\[
 \sup_m\|\widetilde Y_m-Y_m\|_{L^2}\le Ch^{q_\beta}.         \tag{4}
\]
For rank-one operators,
\(\|x\otimes y\|_{\mathrm{HS}}=\|x\|_2\|y\|_2\).  Hence
\[
 \begin{split}
 \|\widetilde\Gamma-\Gamma\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 &\le \|\widetilde\Gamma-\Gamma\|_{\mathrm{HS}}\\
 &\le N_0^{-1}\sum_m
 \{\|\widetilde Y_m-Y_m\|_2\|Y_m\|_2
   +\|\widetilde Y_m\|_2\|\widetilde Y_m-Y_m\|_2\}\\
 &\le C_*h^{q_\beta}.                                      \tag{5}
 \end{split}
\]

Assume \(d>0\).  The canonical donor normalization gives
\[
 \Gamma=N_0^{-1}\sum_mY_m\otimes Y_m
       =\sum_{k=1}^d\sigma_k^2u_k\otimes u_k.               \tag{6}
\]
Thus \(\lambda_d(\Gamma)\ge\gamma_-^2\) and
\(\lambda_{d+1}(\Gamma)=0\).  Also (3) and the normalized factor model show
that \(\widetilde Y_m=(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}b)^\top z_m\), so
\(\operatorname{rank}(\widetilde\Gamma)\le d\).  The variational
characterization of ordered eigenvalues and (5) imply
\[
 |\lambda_k(\widetilde\Gamma)-\lambda_k(\Gamma)|
 \le\|\widetilde\Gamma-\Gamma\|_{\mathrm{op}}.              \tag{7}
\]
For all sufficiently fine grids, (5)--(7) give
\(\lambda_d(\widetilde\Gamma)\ge\gamma_-^2/2\); together with the rank
bound, this proves that \(\widetilde\Gamma\) has exactly \(d\) positive
eigenvalues.

Let \(\mathscr C\) be a fixed contour separating
\([\gamma_-^2/2,2\gamma_+^2]\) from a neighborhood of zero.  Finite-rank
spectral calculus and the resolvent identity give
\[
 \widetilde\Pi-\Pi
 =\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_{\mathscr C}
 (z-\widetilde\Gamma)^{-1}(\widetilde\Gamma-\Gamma)
 (z-\Gamma)^{-1}\,dz.                                      \tag{8}
\]
The two resolvents on \(\mathscr C\) are bounded only by the fixed spectral
gap.  Equations (5) and (8) yield
\[
 \|\widetilde\Pi-\Pi\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le Ch^{q_\beta}.        \tag{9}
\]
Applying the same contour identity with the analytic function \(z^{1/2}\)
on the positive spectral component shows that the selected positive square
roots differ by at most \(Ch^{q_\beta}\) in operator norm.  Choose
orthonormal coordinate frames for the two selected ranges and align them
by the polar factor of their cross-Gram matrix.  Equation (9) makes that
cross-Gram matrix invertible, and the polar identity supplies an orthogonal
matrix \(R_{\mathcal G}\) for which
\[
 \max_p\|\widetilde b_p-R_{\mathcal G}^{\top}b_p\|_{L^2}
 \le Ch^{q_\beta}.                                         \tag{10}
\]
This formulation is insensitive to internal eigenvalue ties.

By the pre-contrast Gram assumption,
\(\lambda_{\min}(H_0)\ge\kappa_-\).  From (10), the factor envelope, and
\(xx^\top-yy^\top=(x-y)x^\top+y(x-y)^\top\),
\[
 \|\widetilde H_0-R_{\mathcal G}^{\top}H_0R_{\mathcal G}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le Ch^{q_\beta}.                                         \tag{11}
\]
For a sufficiently fine grid the right side is at most \(\kappa_-/2\),
so \(\lambda_{\min}(\widetilde H_0)\ge\kappa_-/2\).  Finally,
\[
 A^{-1}-B^{-1}=A^{-1}(B-A)B^{-1}                           \tag{12}
\]
with \(A=\widetilde H_0\) and
\(B=R_{\mathcal G}^{\top}H_0R_{\mathcal G}\) proves the asserted inverse
bound.

It remains to identify the comparison curve.  Linearity of
\(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\) and the normalized factor model give, for the
same target loading,
\[
 \widetilde S^0_{p,\star}-\widetilde s_p
 =\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}(b_p^\top z_\star).                \tag{13}
\]
The interpolated pre-factor Gram is nonsingular by (11), so the population
least-squares step recovers the coordinates of \(z_\star\) in the rotated
interpolated factor basis exactly.  Substitution in the post-period factor
map yields
\[
 \begin{split}
 \theta^{\mathrm{pop}}_{r,\mathcal G}
 &=\widetilde s_1+\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}(b_1^\top z_\star)\\
 &=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}(s_1+b_1^\top z_\star)
 =\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\theta.                            \tag{14}
 \end{split}
\]
Equation (2) at the knots proves the asserted grid equality.  When \(d=0\),
every factor calculation is an empty sum, and (14) reduces to
\(\theta^{\mathrm{pop}}_{1,\mathcal G}=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}s_1\).
\(\square\)

statements.statement: In the general adaptation problem \(\mathcal A_0\subset\mathcal A\) with loss \(D\), Carpentier, Klopp, L\"offler, and Nickl define the minimax testing radius \(\rho_n\) by uniformly consistent tests of \(\mathcal A_0\) against \(\{f\in\mathcal A:D(f,\mathcal A_0)\ge L\rho_n\}\).  Their Theorem~2.1 states that if \(r_n(\mathcal A_0)=o(\rho_n)\), honest adaptation is impossible and every honest confidence set has expected \(D\)-diameter at least a constant multiple of \(\rho_n\) somewhere on \(\mathcal A_0\), under the displayed error-level restriction.

The construction centers at the oracle estimator and chooses the radius \(r_n(\mathcal A)\Psi_n+r_n(\mathcal A_0)(1-\Psi_n)\); its coverage proof separately treats the null, alternatives far from the null, and alternatives within the testing radius.

For any probability measures \(\mathbb P\) and \(\mathbb Q\) with
\(\mathbb P\ll\mathbb Q\), total variation and relative entropy satisfy
\[
\operatorname{TV}(\mathbb P,\mathbb Q)
\leq\left\{\frac12D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\mathbb P\|\mathbb Q)\right\}^{1/2}.
\]

Han and Shah's Theorem~1 structural model requires a finite-dimensional survival factorization \(S^{(0)}_{p,m}(t)=\langle u_p(t),v_m\rangle\) and, separately, inclusion of each treated-unit factor \(v_\star\) in the linear span of the donor factors.  The well-conditioned finite-grid pre-period matrix and latent time-period span restrictions are introduced later as Assumptions~7 and~8 for their Theorem~2, not as conditions of their Theorem~1.
